profiles.summary: The official node still gives the specified word for all 185,529 battery and targeted vectors at head about 52,231,000, and it still runs Cancun without CLZ. The archive client nanoreth published release nb-20261125-2 on 25 November 2026, which moves it from the revm 29 fork to revm 43.0.3 and ruint 1.20.1, but the only public archive endpoint still runs nb-20261110 (f0cad31). No ruint or revm release has appeared since the versions cycle 17 read.

deltas.delta: nanoreth release nb-20261125-2 (commit b92ad36, 25 November 2026) upgrades reth to v2.8.1 with revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, revm-context-interface 43.0.2 and ruint 1.20.1, enables revm memory_limit, and its Cargo.lock equals the master lock read in cycle 17. The previous tag nb-20261110 (f0cad31), which rpc.purroofgroup.com still reports, pins revm 29.0.1 from the hl-archive-node fork fdf9b16 and ruint 1.16.0.

The official node and the testnet node still answer CLZ (0x1e) with NotActivated, and the Prague precompile addresses 0x0b, 0x11 and 0x0100 have no code and return empty, so no EVM fork past Cancun is active or staged on testnet.

profiles.summary: nanoreth now states that receipts of HyperCore system transactions are not covered by the header receipts root, and its new release adds its own commitment to them. The archive client clears transient storage between two transactions of one simulated block. The PoolManager nonce is still 1, so no system transaction has been sent in its name.

deltas.delta: nanoreth pull request 169, merged 25 November 2026: system transaction receipts are not covered by the header receipts root; the release stores a commitment keccak256(rlp([[tx_type, success, cumulative_gas_used, logs], ...])) from the block source and fails the block on a mismatch, and blocks without a commitment run unchecked.

eth_simulateV1 on the archive client with two calls in one block: the first stores 0x2a in transient slot 7 and returns it, the second, a separate transaction to the same contract, loads slot 7 and gets 0. The official and testnet endpoints answer eth_simulateV1 with Method not found.

profiles.summary: sendToEvmWithData makes HyperCore call coreReceiveWithData on the linked token contract, and from the next network upgrade that call gets at most 200,000 gas. The authorizeAqav2Role action carries only a token index and a role, so the address that takes the role is not named in the action.

deltas.delta: sendToEvmWithData calls coreReceiveWithData(from, destinationRecipient, destinationChainId, amount, nonce, data) on the linked contract instead of transfer; the announcement of 19 November 2026 caps its gas at 200,000.

authorizeAqav2Role has the fields token and role ("technical" or "treasury") and no address; the aligned quote assets page says activation follows a validator vote after both deployers have staked and sent the authorization transactions from the staking accounts.

findings.title: HyperCore sends unsigned transfers in the name of addresses that never signed, including a contract, and the record that names such an address is outside the deployer's documented action
findings.difference: HyperCore places unsigned system transactions at the top of HyperEVM blocks and states their sender itself. Under AQAv2 it sends token transfers in the name of the linked contract and of a treasury address. The receipts of these transactions are not covered by the header receipts root. On Ethereum a balance leaves an address only through a transaction that address signed or a call made by its own code.
findings.mechanism: If HyperCore recorded the PoolManager as the treasury address of an aligned quote asset, the node would send transfer calls on that token with the PoolManager as msg.sender. The token balance would fall while pool state, ERC-6909 balances and protocol fee counters keep counting it as owed, because the PoolManager reads a balance only between sync and settle inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). The last takes in that token would then revert inside the transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-88). New in this cycle: the authorizeAqav2Role action has only a token index and a role, and the documentation says the authorization transactions come from the deployers' staking accounts, so the action that binds a role names no address and the rule by which the treasury address is chosen is still unpublished. nanoreth pull request 169 states that system transaction receipts are outside the header receipts root, so before release nb-20261125-2 no public client compared them. The PoolManager nonce is still 1 on the official and archive endpoints, so no system transaction has used it as sender. An ordinary account cannot create the record: it needs two staked deployers of 500,000 HYPE each and a validator vote.
findings.impact: All pools and ERC-6909 claims in a token for which HyperCore named the PoolManager as the rebalancing address. Nothing is exposed today.
findings.preconditions: The validator set, or whatever privileged record names an AQAv2 treasury, must name the PoolManager. An ordinary account cannot.
findings.mitigations: Watch the PoolManager nonce, which rises with any system transaction sent in its name, and run nanoreth nb-20261125-2 or later, which checks system transaction receipts against the block source. Ask the Hyperliquid team whether the node refuses an address with code as AQAv2 treasury.

cleared.result: No mismatch and no error in either set, so MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMPI, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD and the mulDiv and divRoundingUp compositions used by FullMath, UnsafeMath and SqrtPriceMath still return the specified words.

cleared.check: Rerun of pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py for chain 999 against Ethereum.
cleared.result: pmdiff.py (250 scripts): HyperEVM returns the same bytes as Ethereum on 250 scripts, 0 differ, 0 errors; pmdiff2.py (300 scripts): HyperEVM returns the same bytes as Ethereum on 299 scripts, 1 differ (script indexes [189]), 0 errors. The one differing script, index 189 of pmdiff2, is the same index that differed in cycle 17 and in opcodes/pmdiff2.json, a swap that runs out of the 30 million gas the endpoint grants a simulated call.

cleared.check: L-896: can mined swaps reach the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:40-52)? The fallback runs only on the exact input token0 path (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:147, src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:78) and needs amount times sqrtPX96 of at least 2^256 - 2^224; with sqrtPX96 below 2^160 that needs an amount of at least 2^95, and the amount passed is never above the token0 the swap paid.
cleared.result: Screen of all Swap events of the v3, Algebra and PoolManager layouts in blocks 52,031,000 to 52,231,000: 389,589 Swap events (389,257 of the v3 and Algebra 1.0/1.1 layout, 331 of the Algebra 1.2 layout, 1 of the PoolManager), 0 with |amount0| at or above 2^95, and the largest |amount0| times logged sqrtPrice is below 2^175. No mined swap comes within reach of the fallback, so the closed validator's result on that branch cannot be checked from mined data; the branch is covered by the opcode vectors and the reference interpreter.

cleared.check: L-825: does the Debug form of HaltReason in the official node error texts (EVM error: InvalidJump) date its reth or revm generation?
cleared.result: No. reth v1.3.0, v1.6.0, v1.8.0, v2.0.0 and v2.8.1 declare EvmHalt(HaltReason) with the format "EVM error: {0:?}", and v2.9.0, v2.10.0, v2.11.0 and main store format!("{err:?}") in EvmHalt(String). Every release in that range prints the Debug form, so the text carries no version information.

cleared.check: Did the nanoreth or hyper-evm-sync dependency pins change since cycle 17, and what does nb-20261125-2 change on the opcode path?
cleared.result: hyper-evm-sync main Cargo.lock is byte identical to the cycle 17 copy. nanoreth master and nb-20261125-2 have the cycle 17 lock; Cargo.toml only adds the jemalloc and js-tracer features, which are allocator and RPC tracer options. The release notes list sync, RPC, receipt check and compliance fixes and no change to EVM execution apart from the reth and revm upgrade that cycle 17 read.

cleared.check: L-415 for HyperEVM: is transient storage cleared between two transactions of one block?
cleared.result: On the archive client a simulated block of two transactions shows the second reading 0 from the slot the first wrote. The official endpoint does not serve eth_simulateV1. Cycle 17 traced all 2,782 PoolManager transactions and found none that ends with an ERC-20 still synced, so no mined pair of the kind the lead asks for exists, and every mined block replays.

cleared.check: sendToEvmWithData and its 200,000 gas cap: can an ordinary account make HyperCore move PoolManager funds or bracket its own sync and settle with the delivery?
cleared.result: The action calls coreReceiveWithData on the linked token contract as a system transaction ahead of the signed transactions of the block, so it cannot run between a user's sync and settle (transient state is per transaction, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). It moves tokens out of the system address, not out of the PoolManager. A smaller gas cap only makes the delivery fail sooner. A delivery addressed to the PoolManager credits nobody and is the stranded payment pattern of F-021.

cleared.check: The 1 USDC minimum for HyperEVM to HyperCore transfers.
cleared.result: A take of USDC to the USDC system address below 1 USDC is lost to the caller who chose that recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297); it debits that caller and no one else. Token and recipient hazard, recorded in one line.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks: every HyperEVM change announced for the next six months.
cleared.result: The announced items are HyperEVM error responses that include HyperCore errors (RPC only), the 200,000 gas cap of sendToEvmWithData, and HyperCore trading changes. No EVM fork past Cancun is announced, and testnet still refuses CLZ and has no Prague precompiles. None of these changes an opcode result, transient storage, the call semantics the PoolManager uses or who can move its balances.

cleared.check: Mined PoolManager activity since the cycle 17 head and swaps.py for chain 999.
cleared.result: Only 33 Initialize logs since block 52,194,939. swaps.py on its window found 7 swaps, all 7 with the exact tick relation and both consecutive pairs matching the single-step exact input case.

leads.question: Did hl-node itself move to a revm 43 generation together with nanoreth nb-20261125-2, which the team asked nanoreth operators to run for compatibility with hl-node, and does any public endpoint now serve that build?
leads.why: From that point the public replay clients run two interpreter generations (revm 29 fork and revm 43) against a closed validator whose version is unknown, and each should be compared with the reference once reachable.

leadResults.answer: No mined swap reaches the fallback. blocks 52,031,000 to 52,231,000: 389,589 Swap events (389,257 of the v3 and Algebra 1.0/1.1 layout, 331 of the Algebra 1.2 layout, 1 of the PoolManager), 0 with |amount0| at or above 2^95, and the largest |amount0| times logged sqrtPrice is below 2^175. The fallback needs an amount of at least 2^95 on the exact input token0 path, so mined data gives no instance and none is close.

The build is now released as nb-20261125-2 (25 November 2026, revm 43.0.3, ruint 1.20.1), but rpc.purroofgroup.com still reports reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 and no other public endpoint found answers as nanoreth, so the battery and traces could not be run on it.

Every reth release read from v1.3.0 to main prints HaltReason in Debug form in eth_call errors ("EVM error: {0:?}" before v2.9.0, format!("{err:?}") after). The fingerprint does not bound the generation.

Privileged actor. authorizeAqav2Role carries only token and role and is sent from the deployers' staking accounts; no published rule says whether the treasury address must sign. F-020 stays plausible at operator level.
Privileged actor. Same evidence as L-884; no published rule on changing the designation after activation.
Privileged actor. No proof of control by the treasury address is documented, and none is excluded.
Privileged actor. The CoreWriter action table (ids 1 to 17, no 14) still has no AQAv2 action, and the exchange action names no address.
Privileged actor. Same as L-116; the PoolManager nonce is still 1, so no system transaction has used it as sender.

For HyperEVM: the archive client clears transient storage between two transactions of one simulated block, the official endpoint lacks eth_simulateV1, and no mined block holds the pair because no PoolManager transaction ever ended with an ERC-20 synced. The other chains belong to other units.
